approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local structural changes. After receiving real scores, it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move is worse than the current state. Exact score ties currently go to the lexically first canonical identity. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms when several accepted neighbors share the exact maximum score, then use the existing canonical ordering if sizes also tie. This lets the walk avoid some neutral graph growth without surrendering the best score available in that accepted batch. Earlier siblings changed edit generation or structural memory; the whole-branch deletion child exposed smaller proposals but often lost score and later regrew. This mechanism instead acts on an already scored tie set. It adds no deletion operator, chemistry filter or size preference outside exact maximum ties.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes all supplied replicas with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its actual per-seed summaries and run logs agree on successful completion. A passive audit of all 435 saved accepted transitions, joined to their recorded trajectories, finds 26 batches with multiple exact accepted-score maxima, containing 64 maximizer candidates; 409 batches have a unique maximum. Of the 26 ties, 16 match their source score, five improve it and five worsen it. Seven maximum-tie sets contain different heavy-atom counts. In three of those sets, the canonical lexical winner is one heavy atom larger than an equally scoring alternative: seed 0 deco_hop batches 14 and 18, and seed 2 deco_hop batch 10. The other 23 ties need no winner change under the proposed rule. Thus the Parent sometimes adds an atom on a score plateau solely because of canonical ordering, despite an accepted maximum of smaller size. This is a sparse demonstrated selection opportunity, not evidence that every tied score is a batch maximum or that smaller future states score better. The complete read-only counts, exact identities and log/trajectory receipts are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-03-improve-L16.plan-tie-audit.json. The related compactness evidence n-0e56e71777c4 reports 69 evaluated whole-branch prunings, only four selected next states, subsequent regrowth in all four, and paired macro loss -0.06428301128179302. That result motivates requiring an actual score tie before giving size any decision authority; it does not establish a benefit for the present rule.
hypothesis: Resolve exact ties at the maximum accepted batch score by choosing the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms, then the lexicographically smallest canonical identity, while leaving every non-tied accepted maximum and the independent best archive unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Six compact tie choices preserved immediate scores, but the panel mean fell
finding_summary.insights: Equal immediate scores do not make tied molecules equivalent starting points for the remaining search. The rule reached smaller real states and preserved the independent archive, so the missing score benefit cannot be explained by a tie implementation failure or an immediate sacrifice in accepted score. The two affected walks ended smaller than their parents yet found lower best scores, narrowing the claim: this size preference controls some neutral growth, but has not identified better future neighborhoods. The chemistry assessment reinforces the distinction between atom count and useful simplification: deco_hop proposals had slightly fewer atoms on average but greater molecular mass and more nitrogen-halogen bonds, while unusual sulfur chemistry persisted. A compact winner can also be a bond change or element substitution. Local chemical organization or neighborhood quality therefore remains a more informative open question than size alone. Six interventions in two overlapping walks do not isolate the contribution of each choice, and the sparse activation does not establish how the rule would behave on other tasks.
finding_summary.results: Six of 28 exact maximum-score ties selected a different molecule, all on deco_hop plateaus in two seeds. Every changed choice preserved the accepted maximum score and used one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner, saving ten atoms across those decisions. Three choices kept the source size and three reduced it by one atom. All 407 unique maxima retained the same choice on the same accepted batch, and the identity, archive and transition audits passed. Descendants exceeded the compact selected size after five of the six changes; the remaining case finished at that size after five further steps. Later archive improvements occurred, but the complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655, a paired loss of 0.001104 against the required gain of 0.002. Both affected seeds declined; all four other tasks and the third seed retained exactly the parent's molecule/score sequences.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often aromatic molecules with recurrent unusual sulfur, reactive halogen bonds and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-770a3cefca6a covers every task in the supplied digest; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The digest contains 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Its proposal ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0 and describes the presence of aromatic SMILES tokens, not the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. These are substantial heterocyclic and polycyclic graphs, not small acyclic fragments. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing of all 4350 proposals succeeds: they contain 21-49 heavy atoms, with median 33, and 2-10 perceived rings, with median 4. Graph parsing does not establish energetic stability or a synthesis. Relatively conventional indole carboxamides coexist with heavily decorated nitrogen heterocycles, sulfur-rich cages, medium-ring bridges, heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual neutral sulfur multiple bonding. Some individual structures are plausible, but repeated problematic chemistry among the reported high scorers and late proposals supports the overall implausible/weak reading. Diversity is moderate at the graph level across the panel; high scorers within a task frequently remain closely related members of a local family. All proposal charged_rate and stereocentre_rate counters are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or stereochemical labels, not an absence of ionizable atoms or stereogenic graphs: 3432 proposals have potential unassigned stereocentres in the passive audit. Against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, all molecule/score sequences match exactly on four tasks; only deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 differ. The chemistry comparison below concerns those observed outputs and makes no activation finding. All descriptor counts and parent comparisons are reproducible in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-03-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json; they describe proposal occurrences, and perceived ring counts can include overlapping rings in bridged systems. The digest final_molecules are the last proposal records from seed 2, not a selected endpoint or the best archive.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms, median 25. Their characteristic chemistry is an indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene joined through an amide or ketone to an aryl group, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, thiol and halogen substituents. The cited 0.39905049777278273 indole carboxamide is a relatively conventional 23-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring molecule bearing ethoxy, methyl and thiol groups. The 0.41003927643747895 best example has 26 heavy atoms and the same perceived aromatic ring count, but is a benzofuran with an N-chloroamide, an amino/chloro-substituted benzylic carbon, an aniline and a thiol. The 0.393567030299894 example is a benzothiophene aryl ketone with an aminomethoxy arm and chloromethyl group. Late seed-2 proposals instead include bridged unsaturated sulfur heterocycles with an amino-ketone linker; the last proposal scores 0.3852230774700024. All supplied molecule/score sequences are identical to the parent.
liabilities: The best benzofuran combines an N-chloroamide and an amino-bearing benzylic chloride; these create chemical-reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary aryl substitution pattern.

Thiol, chloromethyl and N-fluoro/N-hydroxy functionality occurs in the cited series; the last sulfur-bridged proposal additionally contains an N-N linkage. These motifs need individual chemical scrutiny rather than treating sanitized graphs as equally makeable.
missing_features: Sustained coverage of chemically conventional variants of the observed compact carbonyl-linked aromatic motif is incomplete: it appears among the stronger examples, but later proposals often deform the rings and linker or introduce unusual sulfur chemistry.

The best example lacks a defined configuration at its amino/chloro-substituted benzylic centre. A score benefit from resolving that configuration is untested; the records do not identify an additional required target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The stronger cited molecules retain a carbonyl-linked aromatic framework while changing its substituents. At 0.021532846118034143, the cited low example retains an aryl ketone but replaces the compact fused aromatic core with a partly saturated, enlarged ring system; it has only one perceived aromatic ring. At 0.03343008011310944, another low example retains three aromatic rings but replaces the amide carbonyl with a substituted saturated carbon. Together these observations associate higher scores with both carbonyl linkage and compact conjugated-ring organization, rather than aromaticity alone. The strongest example still contains reactive-looking groups, so the gradient does not demonstrate a preference for synthetic plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: These are large decorated heteroaromatics: 30-49 heavy atoms, median 38, with aromatic tokens in every proposal. The 0.6145389662714401 best family carries a fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyl/thiocarbonyl groups, a densely substituted benzylamino aryl group, imines, fluorinated arms and a sulfur-containing ester side chain. The first cited best molecule has 46 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 800.601. One equally scoring variant contains sulfur triple-bonded to carbon on both sides. Late seed-2 molecules retain carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles but add polyunsaturated ether arms, N-bromination and sulfur-oxygen linkers; the cited hydroperoxide-bearing proposal scores 0.5518599963349826. This is the only task whose sequences differ from the parent, in seeds 0 and 2. Across its proposals, mean heavy atoms change from 38.90344827586207 to 38.60344827586207, while calculated mean molecular weight changes from 597.9077586206896 to 618.5739229885057. N-halogen occurrences change from 33 to 161 and S-halogen occurrences from 180 to 217. The atom-count change therefore does not describe a general improvement in the observed chemical quality.
liabilities: The cited best molecules contain unusual neutral carbon-sulfur triple-bond environments, a sulfenyl chloride, imines and extensive mixed halogenation. A molecular graph of this form is not a demonstrated stable synthetic product.

N-brominated heterocycles, a hydroperoxide, long polyunsaturated arms and sulfur-oxygen linkers occur in the late digest. Large molecular weight and flexible decoration remain substantial liabilities even when heavy-atom count is slightly lower than the parent mean.
missing_features: Chemically conventional, lower-mass decoration alternatives that retain the recurring carbonyl/heteroaromatic framework are poorly represented among the best examples; added branch length, sulfur and halogens dominate instead.

The strongest recorded plateau supplies no evidence for which missing decoration would improve the objective. What is missing chemically is stable bonding and controlled side-chain complexity within that scaffold family, not demonstrated access to a specific unseen target structure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic ester/phenol and fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. The cited low ring-rewired example scores 0.526081691583997. Higher-scoring examples preserve a related heterocyclic framework while extensively modifying and enlarging the decorations. The best score 0.6145389662714401 is shared by the cited single- and double-carbon-triple-bonded sulfur variants, so this observed plateau does not distinguish sharply different sulfur bonding. It supports tolerance of these decoration changes, not evidence that sulfur hypervalence is chemically beneficial. Within the late seed-2 series, the more aromatic carbonyl-bearing 0.5942930760374979 example exceeds the hydroperoxide/carbonyl-disrupted 0.5518599963349826 example, although their side chains also differ. Parent versus child observed maxima are 0.6161710037174721 versus 0.6145389662714401 for seed 0 and 0.6092182584436399 versus 0.5942930760374979 for seed 2; the smaller mean graph size did not accompany better maxima in these observed outputs.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms, median 36, and typically combine halogenated aryl groups, phenols, amine-bearing rings and sulfur-rich linkers or bridges. Every proposal has aromatic tokens; halogen_rate is 0.9966. The 0.9148143511682032 best example has 32 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, including two aromatic rings, a tertiary aliphatic ring nitrogen, an aminomethyl substituent and an aryl-bound ring nitrogen. Its scaffold also contains unusual sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding. The 0.8856242185485628 example has an aziridine, an amino-substituted saturated nitrogen ring, a sulfur-sulfur double-bond unit and halogenated phenol/aryl groups. These are substantial amine-bearing frameworks, not a generator lacking ring amines. All supplied molecule/score sequences match the parent.
liabilities: Neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding, hydrogen-bearing sulfur in unusual multiple-bond environments and a strained aziridine make the high-scoring series chemically questionable.

Heavy halogenation and complex ring topology accompany undefined configurations. Every proposal has at least one potential unassigned stereocentre in the passive audit, despite stereocentre_rate 0.0 in the digest.
missing_features: Conventional, less reactive realizations of the observed aryl-plus-nonacylated-amine arrangement are missing from the cited best family: the aromatic and amine motifs are entangled with unusual sulfur bonds and, in another high example, an aziridine.

Explicit molecular-state definition is missing despite the amines and stereogenic rings. The best example has four potential unassigned stereocentres; the neutral SMILES do not establish protonation at an assay condition, and no score benefit from state enumeration is shown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited 0.007468397818197266 low example is a large aromatic carboxylic acid bearing amide and N-sulfonyl nitrogen functionality, with no conventional nonacylated aliphatic amine by the passive structural heuristic. Stronger cited molecules instead contain free aliphatic amine centres and retain aryl/phenolic surfaces. A closer comparison is the 0.8663008496126992 example and the 0.04252669549740123 late proposal: replacing the attached carbon of its chlorophenyl ring with sulfur destroys that ring aromaticity while retaining the surrounding amine-rich scaffold, and accompanies a large score decrease. Removing the methylene between a tertiary nitrogen and its sulfur-containing ring produces the cited 0.3331237338421948 proposal. Thus the observed gradient is sensitive to ring identity and connection geometry, not simply nitrogen count. The sulfur liabilities persist at high scores; these trajectories alone establish neither binding contacts nor measured affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 27-45 heavy atoms, median 35, and aromatic tokens throughout. The best family is a bridged azaaromatic/aryl framework with alkyl substituents, an N-methyl lactam and a cyclic N-O linkage. The 0.21196904390980506 example has 31 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and a dense network with seven overlapping perceived rings, including medium-sized loops; it has three potential unassigned stereocentres. Other seeds produce much heavier brominated aryl/sulfur/amine derivatives or sulfur-bridged lactam/polyether frameworks. The last seed-2 proposal is a 40-heavy-atom sulfur-rich, carbonyl-bearing polycycle with alcohol/ether/thiol substituents and score 0.18220097615153677. All supplied molecule/score sequences match the parent.
liabilities: Multiple overlapping medium-sized rings and a cyclic N-O bond complicate plausible synthesis and stereochemical control; the perceived ring count should not be mistaken for seven independent ordinary rings.

The cited low brominated molecule includes an O-Br bond, bromomethyl thioether and crowded sulfur environment. Late proposals include hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur and sulfur-carbon multiple bonds. These are chemically distinct liabilities despite retaining aromatic and carbonyl groups.
missing_features: The stronger aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is not represented by a broad set of simpler, synthetically interpretable scaffold alternatives. The top family achieves it through a complicated bridged N-O/lactam network.

Defined configurations and matched alternatives with simpler bridge connectivity are absent from the cited top series. The records do not demonstrate that adding more amines, halogens or ring closures would fill an objective-specific gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic scores 0.1678386594791329. The cited open-chain urea-related derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while the bridged azaaromatic/lactam family reaches 0.21196904390980506. The shorter alkyl-substituent analogue at 0.2087472610464947 and the best example at 0.21196904390980506 differ by a local alkyl extension, consistent with small substituent effects within that family. A much heavier brominated sulfur derivative scores only 0.12870267321446027. The observed association favors this particular connected aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over the shown opened analogues or indiscriminate heavy decoration. It does not establish that arbitrary extra rings are rewarded, or reveal the exact feature needed beyond the best observed score.

per_task.generated_character: These are relatively compact by atom count but highly interconnected sulfur-rich graphs: 25-33 heavy atoms, median 29, and median six perceived rings. The aromatic-token rate is 0.7184; late seed-2 proposals are entirely nonaromatic, so abundant ring closures do not imply abundant aromaticity here. The 0.5903526424693334 best molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms, three fluorines, six perceived rings and seven potential unassigned stereocentres. It contains a carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycle, a fluorohydrin thioether substituent and a heavily bridged sulfur framework. The 0.5527071687189122 analogue has a related four-sulfur cage and eight potential unassigned stereocentres. The last seed-2 proposal instead has an aldehyde, ketone and N-fluoro amidine-like group in a nonaromatic sulfur cage with nine perceived rings. All supplied molecule/score sequences match the parent.
liabilities: Sulfur-carbon multiple bonding at multiply connected neutral sulfur atoms, sulfur-sulfur links, hydrogen-bearing sulfur centres, and small rings embedded in dense cages make the representative best structures synthetically implausible without much stronger chemical evidence.

The late proposals add an aldehyde, N-F bonding and, in the 0.004199910554494925 example, an S-Cl bond. The final graph has eleven potential unassigned stereocentres, so low heavy-atom count does not mean low chemical complexity.
missing_features: Chemically conventional ways of combining the observed fluorinated, carbonyl-rich heteroatom pattern with compact size are missing from the best family. Compactness is realized through densely bridged sulfur chemistry rather than a clearly tractable scaffold.

Stereochemical definition is absent precisely where the graphs are most stereochemically complex. The best and late examples have multiple potential configurations, but the supplied records do not show a score benefit from any particular stereoisomer or an absent free amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited early aromatic ester/dicarbonyl molecule scores 7.590554525032884e-10, while the fluorinated carbonyl/sulfur-cage family reaches 0.5903526424693334. However, an already sulfur-rich, fluorinated, six-perceived-ring example still scores 1.0546805269255595e-09. Sulfur abundance and ring count alone therefore do not explain the gradient. In the final seed-2 batch, the cited 26-heavy-atom cage scores 0.4484554129767839; an expanded lactone-containing neighbour scores 0.2536619453071564, and the sulfenyl-chloride-containing carbonyl derivative scores 0.004199910554494925. The shown scores are sensitive to precise connectivity and atom/functional-group balance. They provide no evidence that these unusual sulfur environments are makeable or that a specific absent medicinal motif would improve the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high-score molecules include carbon-sulfur-carbon connectivity with sulfur triple-bonded on both sides, neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur in multiply connected ring systems. These occur in graphs that parse successfully, including a recorded 0.6145389662714401 plateau that does not distinguish markedly different sulfur bond orders. The issue is the local bonding environment, not every sulfur-containing group.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable control of chemically conventional sulfur bonding while exploring otherwise useful heteroatom patterns.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand access to conventional heteroatom and linker alternatives while retaining the surrounding scaffold, and distinguish unusual sulfur environments from ordinary thioethers, thiocarbonyls and oxidized sulfur groups. Chemical validity needs information beyond successful graph sanitization; the same chemical criterion must apply to every supplied objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Passive graph reading finds N-halogen bonds in 628 proposals, O-halogen bonds in 301 and S-halogen bonds in 333 out of 4350 proposals; these categories can overlap. Digest exemplars show N-chloroamides, N-brominated carbonyl heterocycles, O-brominated aryl substituents and sulfenyl chlorides. Some of these liabilities coexist with the highest recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen placement is insufficiently selective for stable medicinal substituents rather than reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent halogen edits with their attachment chemistry intact, and offer matched conventional carbon-bound substitutions or replacements for reactive heteroatom attachments. Use the observed local scores to explore those alternatives without assuming that generic halogen presence is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the changed proposal family, parent-to-child mean heavy atoms decrease from 38.90344827586207 to 38.60344827586207 while calculated mean molecular weight increases from 597.9077586206896 to 618.5739229885057. Elsewhere, a cited 30-heavy-atom high scorer carries five sulfur atoms and six perceived rings, and a 31-heavy-atom high scorer has a network of seven overlapping perceived rings. The recorded chemistry decouples small atom count from tractability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Compact graph size does not reliably produce lower molecular mass, simpler ring topology or easier synthesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically complete simplifications and scaffold alternatives that can reduce heavy-element burden, bridge congestion or flexible decoration while retaining observed aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships. Evaluate chemical simplicity independently of heavy-atom count; no supplied comparison establishes a score gain from a blanket size preference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive perception nevertheless identifies potential unassigned stereocentres in 3432 of 4350 proposals. Cited high-score molecules include graphs with four and seven potential unassigned centres, and a cited final cage has eleven. Thus the missing labels are a molecular-definition gap, not evidence that the search only makes achiral molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry for many graphs with potential stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly represent stereochemical choices when edits create, retain or remove stereogenic centres, using only task-independent molecular information and the permitted identity rules. This would improve the specificity of the output; the observed trajectories do not establish a score advantage for stereoisomer enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited comparisons include a compact carbonyl-linked fused aromatic family above enlarged or carbonyl-disrupted variants, and an amine-rich aryl framework whose ring-dearomatized sulfur analogue scores much lower. The top exemplars repeatedly remain within one local structural family, often adding unusual sulfur bonds or bridge congestion. Rings and aliphatic amine centres are already present; their stable arrangement in alternative scaffolds is the incomplete capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships are insufficiently explored through diverse conventional scaffold alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer scaffold and linker changes that preserve chemically interpretable arrangements of aromatic surfaces, carbonyls and nonacylated amines while changing ring topology or attachment geometry. Let real feedback determine where those arrangements matter; the evidence supports richer conventional alternatives, not a universal pharmacophore or a task-specific motif prescription.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
